title: Establishing the Benefit a Rider Has Already Paid in the Benefit Year
content:
Reconciliation basis for the benefit-year accumulator on the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders. The figure a rider record shows used toward the benefit year's maximum and the lines that rider has settled do not always agree, and the basis below settles which is taken.

## The rule

**Where a reversal stands on the member's benefit history against a settled line**, the benefit already paid in the benefit year is what the rider paid on the lines it has settled in the benefit year less what those reversals backed out.

**Where no such reversal stands and the figure the rider record shows used toward the benefit year's maximum is not what the rider paid on the lines it has settled in the benefit year**, the benefit already paid in the benefit year is what the rider paid on those settled lines.

**Otherwise**, the benefit already paid in the benefit year is the figure the rider record shows used toward the benefit year's maximum.

## What the three quantities are

**The figure the record shows.** The running figure the rider record itself carries as used toward the benefit year's maximum.

**What the rider paid on the lines it has settled.** What the rider paid, taken over the lines on the member's benefit history that the rider has settled in the benefit year, whether they stand as paid or as adjusted.

**What the reversals backed out.** What the reversals standing on the member's benefit history carry, each reversal carrying the negative of what the line it applies to had paid.

## Points of judgement

| What the member's benefit history shows | Which figure is taken |
|---|---|
| At least one reversal against a settled line | What the rider paid on the settled lines, less what those reversals backed out |
| No reversal, and the record's figure differs from what the settled lines come to | What the rider paid on those settled lines |
| No reversal, and the record's figure is what the settled lines come to | The figure the record shows |

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

A rider record shows 640.00 USD used toward the benefit year's maximum. The member's benefit history carries settled lines paying 640.00 USD in that benefit year, and one reversal backing out 150.00 USD.

Because a reversal stands against a settled line, the benefit already paid in the benefit year is 640.00 USD less 150.00 USD, that is **490.00 USD** — not the 640.00 USD the record still shows.

Take the same rider with no reversal standing, the record showing 640.00 USD and the settled lines coming to 500.00 USD. The record's figure is not what the settled lines come to, so the benefit already paid is **500.00 USD**.

Take the same rider with no reversal standing, the record showing 500.00 USD and the settled lines also coming to 500.00 USD. The benefit already paid is **500.00 USD**, the figure the record shows.
